properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked with the skill, measured on main's and the branch's binaries) 2026-10-12: no_new_mutually_confusable_pair flagged release_claim/release_report on PR #728 though neither changed — compare_designs' description added the word "in", df moved 125→126 of 197, and a 0.024 margin on release_report's query flipped
properties.source: CI run 38212908193 (reflow2 #728); local --call find_tools on reflow2-mcp 0.83.1 (main) and a debug build of 8ebbc045c; scratchpad ft_rank.sh
properties.statement: ① OBSERVED (CI, workspace job of PR #728 at 8ebbc045c): `1 NEW mutually confusable pair(s): [("release_claim", "release_report")]`; the other four findability tests passed; reproduced locally on the branch (0 passed; 1 failed). Neither tool's text differs from main. ② Searched: fixtures and the test's artifact were found, no prior record of a pair flipping on an unrelated edit. ③ Candidates: (A) compare_designs' longer description shifted document frequency for a query term; (B) a CI-only environment or flakiness; (C) the surface fixture or baseline moved; (D) the longer description changed compare_designs' own rank in one of the two lists (displacement). ④/⑤ Measured: B refuted (fails locally; main's latest CI run on 7213d1ef0 passed this job). C refuted (fixture and baseline untouched on the branch). D refuted (compare_designs is in neither top 6 on either binary). A confirmed: --list-tools --full on both binaries shows one description changed (compare_designs, 881→1035 chars, new words any at budget budget_chars full in list lists lists_shortened long offset over page shortened time with); across both queries' terms only df("in") moved, 125→126; on release_report's query ("what is in this release and is it ready to cut") main ranked pin_at_epoch 5th at 11.682 and release_claim 6th at 11.658, the branch pin_at_epoch 11.638 and release_claim 11.658 (unchanged), so release_claim entered the top 5; release_report was already 5th for release_claim's query (13.518 over claim_report 12.907), making the pair mutual. ⑥ CLASS: the mutual-pair ratchet treats top-5 membership as a stable fact, but term weights are document frequencies over the whole surface, so any description edit anywhere moves every score by a few hundredths, and pairs that close flip on edits unrelated to either tool. The test's text says the baseline only shrinks, so such a flip can only be answered by rewording a description. A faithful replica of the scorer in Python was attempted and was not faithful (it flagged pairs on main that the real test does not), so brittleness across the whole corpus is NOT measured here; what is measured is this pair's margin (0.024) against the shift one common word makes (~0.044 on pin_at_epoch). A stopword floor on term weights was considered and is not recommended from the replica's reading: zeroing common words collapsed many near-ties into more confusable pairs. ⑦ The ratchet test is the failing-first check. ⑧ Contained in c873341c6 (chg:release-claims-description-names-the-claim-it-releases-2026-10-12): release_claim's "releasing what nobody holds" → "releasing a claim nobody holds", its one incidental match with release_report's query; measured after: 11.076 vs pin_at_epoch 11.638 (margin 0.56), still first for its own job. ⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: how many other pairs sit within one common word's shift (needs the real scorer, e.g. the test printing rank-5/6 margins); whether the ratchet should carry a margin floor is a design decision not taken here. Also learned: the build brief's gate list ran tool_confusability.py (top-1 agreement, 195/195) and not the Rust findability tests, so the flip was first seen in CI; a tool-description change must run tests/every_tool_is_found_by_a_query_in_the_users_words.rs.
